authoring.description: UETD-owned MCU-side endpoint state for a project-declared protocol. The protocol defines typed messages, framing, timing, and validity rules; UETD builds the MCU codec and this module tracks link qualification and valid received data. It defines no peer identity handshake, hardware driver, or FPGA RTL.

ports.description: True while the selected MCU transport/protocol reports the external FPGA endpoint as link-qualified.
True after at least one complete validated protocol update and until the protocol timeout, link loss, parser fault, or reset invalidates it.
Receiver-local monotonic timestamp of the most recent complete validated update.

constraints: Freshness is evaluated only in the receiving MCU's monotonic clock domain.
The generated protocol parser reports an update only after its declared framing, sequence, message, transaction, and integrity checks pass.
A link drop or expired protocol validity invalidates cached data before the application can use it.
Message fields and their wire encoding are supplied by the project protocol; this module defines no identity, contract-ID, or contract-hash fields.

operations.description: Update local link qualification from the selected transport/protocol; qualification loss clears cached valid data.

arguments.description: Whether the transport/protocol currently considers the FPGA endpoint link-qualified.

operations.description: Record the receiver-local time of a complete message or transaction after the generated parser validates it.

arguments.description: Monotonic timestamp from the receiving MCU.

operations.description: Invalidate cached peer data after timeout, malformed input, reset, or protocol-defined session loss.
Check the last validated update against an application or protocol age limit using the receiver-local clock.

arguments.description: Current time from the same receiving MCU monotonic clock.
Maximum permitted age for the selected protocol data.

notes: UETD derives typed send/receive message ports from the project's declared protocol and selected .uefs link role.
Every active wire field maps explicitly to a logical-record field; every active message is bound once by a component assignment or operating-system channel.
UETD generates the MCU-side encoder/parser, protocol conversions, and receiver-local message timing from those declarations.
The external FPGA design and its RTL/bitstream remain consumer-authored.
This module does not add a contract-ID/hash handshake or select an identity/hash encoding.
